slides.heading: Longest Subarray With Sum
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Longest Subarray With Sum, a hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Non-negative ints; [start, end] of the longest subarray summing to target, or [] if none.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Non-negative ints; start, end of the longest subarray summing to target, or if none. Sliding window.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Values are non-negative, so a sliding window grows to add and shrinks to subtract.
slides.narration: Values are non-negative, so a sliding window grows to add and shrinks to subtract.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Prefix sums + hash map for negatives
slides.narration: Checking every subarray is quadratic. Since values are non-negative, a sliding window works: grow right, shrink left when the sum is too big, in linear time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Expand the right edge adding values
2. Shrink from the left while the sum is too big
3. Record the longest window equal to target
slides.narration: Step by step. First, expand the right edge adding values. Second, shrink from the left while the sum is too big. Third, record the longest window equal to target.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We grow r, add a r, shrink from l while the sum exceeds target, and record the window when it matches and is longer.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: The window only works because values are non-negative; zeros can extend a match. With negatives, use prefix sums and a hash map.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Mention the prefix-sum and hash-map version for negative numbers.
